entities.summary:
The Citroën is a French automotive manufacturer headquartered in the PSA Poissy Plant, founded in 1919 by André Girard. This institution matters historically as it played a significant role in the development of modern transportation and mass production techniques.

As one of the earliest mass-produced cars, Citroën's innovative designs and engineering helped shape the automotive industry into what it is today. The company's contributions to the development of the automobile, including its pioneering work on hydraulic braking systems, have had a lasting impact on road safety and infrastructure.

The Citroën has also been shaped by significant events in its history, including World War I and II, where the company produced military vehicles and equipment for the French and Allied forces. The post-war period saw Citroën's expansion into new markets and the introduction of new models, cementing its position as a major player in the global automotive industry.
